findings.title: Concurrent-deletion NPE still possible in the other getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: Only getSubGroupsCount() now null-checks the result of modelSupplier.get(). The three getSubGroupsStream(...) overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly. If the group was deleted concurrently, the supplier returns null and these throw the same NPE this PR is meant to fix. Either handle null there (for example return Stream.empty()) or explain why they cannot be reached.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null for a deleted group
findings.body: A vanished group makes getSubGroupsCount() return a null Long instead of throwing. Any caller that unboxes the value, or any other GroupModel consumer, would hit an NPE later and farther from the cause. In GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount the null is passed straight to setSubGroupCount, so the representation silently reports no count for a group that no longer exists. Returning 0L, or skipping groups that no longer exist, would be more predictable. The null-return contract should also be documented.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined and the test is timing-dependent
findings.body: The background reader thread is started and never joined. After deletedAll.set(true), assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty()) can run before the thread's last iteration finishes, so an exception from that iteration could be missed. The thread also runs a tight loop with no bound, and an uncaught Error would not be reported. The test can pass without exercising the race at all, and it asserts only that the list is empty, not which exception occurred. Use an ExecutorService or Thread.join() before asserting, and consider a failure message. The 100 groups created are also not registered for cleanup if the test fails midway.
